newsitem.title: UK: KLM plane crash-lands at London airport, one hurt.
newsitem.headline: KLM plane crash-lands at London airport, one hurt.

text.p: Forty-five passengers and crew escaped serious injury on Sunday when a Dutch passenger plane crash-landed at London's Heathrow airport, airline officials said.
Witnesses credited a quick-thinking pilot with preventing disaster and saving the 41 passengers and four crew.

Three passengers were treated for shock and one for a twisted ankle after the landing gear on the left side of the KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV Fokker 50 aircraft collapsed as the plane touched down, a KLM spokesman said in Amsterdam.
"The left-side landing gear collapsed during the roll-out at a speed of around 100 kilometres (60 miles) per hour," spokesman Peter Wellhuner said.

The pilot earlier reported to the control tower that the left landing gear was failing to engage, but after several manoeuvres and a visual inspection from the ground was ordered to come in to land, Wellhuner added.
One witness said he believed the pilot of the plane, flight KL483 from Rotterdam, had saved the lives of his passengers.
"It was very dramatic -- my legs are still shaking even now," airport security guard Kailash Joshi said.
"I give full credit to the pilot for landing as well as he did considering the circumstances. He definitely saved some lives. I think everyone watching was expecting the worst."
Sherif Fahmy, a 35-year-old businessman from Cairo who was aboard the plane, said he had been terrified.
"As we came in to land, my life flashed before me like a scene from a movie," a clearly shaken Fahmy said afterwards.
"The left-hand wheel wouldn't lock down. We saw it come down as we came in to land the first time and then we had to go up again," Fahmy added.

"He (the pilot) tried to get it down three times and then announced that we would have to make an emergency landing. We had to get into the brace position with our heads down and the crew showed us how to do it. The crew were very cool and that calmed everyone a little bit."
A spokeswoman for Heathrow said the plane had come down on the southern runway, which remained closed.
"This means that all take-offs and landings are on the northern runway which is obviously causing some delays to flights," she said. Hundreds of flights were disrupted.
The Civil Aviation Authority was investigating the incident.
